extracted.intended_audience: federal/state/local government communications officers and agency press/public affairs staff
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting, formatting, and distributing official government press releases that are plain-language, accessible, transparent, and non‑partisan, following GSA best practices and legal accessibility requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain language (Plain Writing Act of 2010)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use plain language as required by the Plain Writing Act of 2010.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target an 8th-grade reading level, use active voice, short sentences (under 25 words), define acronyms on first use, provide concrete examples, and avoid jargon and bureaucratic language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility (Section 508 compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure communications comply with accessibility requirements (Section 508).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a plain text version, include alt text for multimedia, ensure screen reader compatibility, meet color contrast standards, and provide translations for major languages where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency (FOIA-aware)
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications should be transparent and mindful of Freedom of Information Act considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite appropriate authorities in the body and include sufficient factual detail for public understanding and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bipartisan tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt a bipartisan tone in government communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid political framing and partisan language; emphasize service and public benefit rather than promoting a political agenda.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public benefit focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Frame communications around public benefit and service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how actions or announcements benefit the public, not agency self-promotion.

rubrics_metrics.name: No partisan framing
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid partisan framing in messaging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use messaging that could be interpreted as supporting or opposing political parties or candidates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency seal/logo
rubrics_metrics.description: Include the agency seal or logo on the press release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required element for official identification of the issuing agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: "FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE"
rubrics_metrics.description: Include the phrase 'FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE' on the release when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard placement to indicate release timing and distribution status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release number
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a release number on the press release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps with tracking and reference; use agency numbering convention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date
rubrics_metrics.description: Include the date of issuance on the press release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the official date of release for distribution and archival records.

rubrics_metrics.name: City of issuance
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the city (and state) of issuance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard press-release convention; helps localize the announcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline (news + agency action)
rubrics_metrics.description: Write a headline that conveys the news and the agency action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Headline should be clear, news-focused, and indicate what the agency did or is announcing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Body with appropriate authorities cited
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a body that explains the announcement and cites the appropriate legal or policy authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference statutes, regulations, orders, or official program authorities where relevant to support claims or actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quote from senior official
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a quote from a senior official.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a succinct, service-oriented quote that contextualizes the action and its public benefit; attribute the quote to the official and their title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boilerplate (agency mission)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a boilerplate describing the agency mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short standard paragraph about the agency used consistently across releases to describe mission and responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media contact
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide media contact information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include name, phone, email, and any other relevant contact for journalists seeking more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8th-grade reading level target
rubrics_metrics.description: Target an 8th-grade reading level for public-facing text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess readability and simplify language to make content broadly understandable; aligns with plain-language requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Use active voice in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer subject-verb-object constructions to improve clarity and directness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short sentences (under 25 words)
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep sentences short—ideally under 25 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Break complex thoughts into multiple sentences to improve readability and comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define acronyms on first use
rubrics_metrics.description: Spell out and define acronyms the first time they appear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the full phrase followed by the acronym in parentheses, then use the acronym thereafter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concrete examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Use concrete examples to illustrate points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where possible, include specific examples, data, or scenarios so readers understand real-world impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid jargon and bureaucratic language
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid technical jargon and bureaucratic phrasing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replace agency-specific terms with plain-language equivalents that the general public will understand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain text version available
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a plain text version of the press release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures accessibility for assistive technologies and users on low-bandwidth connections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia with alt text
rubrics_metrics.description: Include alt text for multimedia assets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All images and non-text media should have meaningful alt text descriptions for screen reader users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Screen reader compatible
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure pages and documents are compatible with screen readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure content (headings, lists, links) semantically and test with common assistive technologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color contrast standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Meet color contrast standards for text and graphics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow recognized contrast ratios to ensure readability for users with visual impairments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation for major languages
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide translations for major languages where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer translated versions to reach non‑English speaking audiences; prioritize languages relevant to affected communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional but accessible tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt a tone that is professional yet accessible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance official voice with plain language so content is authoritative but understandable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service-oriented tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Frame messaging around service to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize how actions serve citizens rather than agency achievements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public benefit emphasized
rubrics_metrics.description: Highlight the public benefit in messaging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make explicit how the announcement improves public goods, services, safety, or welfare.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid promotional language
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use promotional or marketing-style language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep statements factual and informational rather than saleslike or self-congratulatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy announcements (press release type)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use press releases to announce policy changes or initiatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure such releases to explain policy context, authority, and expected public impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program launches (press release type)
rubrics_metrics.description: Announce launches of new programs via press release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include operational details, eligibility, timelines, and contact points for participation or questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory actions (press release type)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use press releases to communicate regulatory actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite the legal/regulatory authority, effective dates, and any comment/appeal processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service updates (press release type)
rubrics_metrics.description: Announce updates to government services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear information on what changed, who is affected, and how to access services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award announcements (press release type)
rubrics_metrics.description: Publicize awards, grants, or recognitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify recipients, selection criteria, and the award’s purpose and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical reports (press release type)
rubrics_metrics.description: Release statistical reports or data summaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present key findings clearly, include methodology or links to full reports, and provide context for interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crisis/emergency notifications (press release type)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use press releases for crisis or emergency notifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convey urgent, actionable information quickly; prioritize clarity, timing, and authoritative instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency website news section (distribution channel)
rubrics_metrics.description: Publish press releases on the agency website news section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a centralized archive for discoverability and public record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government News Network (distribution channel)
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribute releases via Government News Network.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use interagency or government-specific distribution networks for wider official reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct outreach to congressional offices (distribution channel)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct direct outreach to congressional offices when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide notice and briefings to relevant congressional staff for transparency and coordination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wire syndication (distribution channel)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use wire services for broader distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syndicate to news wires to reach national and local media outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social media (with content moderation) (distribution channel)
rubrics_metrics.description: Share releases or summaries on social media, with moderation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adapt messaging for platform constraints, monitor comments, and moderate according to agency policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sector-specific newsletters (distribution channel)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use sector- or audience-specific newsletters to reach targeted stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor distribution lists to relevant sectors (e.g., industry, state/local partners, advocacy groups).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorities cited
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite appropriate authorities when describing actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include legal, regulatory, or policy references in the body to substantiate agency actions and provide context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senior official quote
rubrics_metrics.description: Include attribution and a quote from a senior official to contextualize the release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quote should be concise, emphasize service/public benefit, and include the official’s title; this is a required element.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multilingual where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide multilingual materials when appropriate for the audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer translations of key communications into major languages relevant to impacted communities to improve reach and equity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service-oriented framing (Quality Rubric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Frame content around service to the public as part of the GSA quality rubric.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize describing public benefit, access to services, and practical outcomes over agency promotion.
